case_number: Civil Appeal Nos. of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 10622-10623 of 2022) and Civil Appeal Nos. of 2022 (Arising out of SLP (C) Nos. 11364-11365 of 2022)
summary: The State of Jharkhand challenged the maintainability of two Public Interest Litigations (PILs) filed by Shiv Shankar Sharma before the Jharkhand High Court, which alleged financial misconduct involving the Soren family and sought investigation by agencies like CBI and ED. The High Court had proceeded with the PILs despite preliminary objections on maintainability. The Supreme Court examined whether the PILs complied with the Jharkhand High Court (Public Interest Litigation) Rules, 2010, particularly Rules 4, 4A, 4B, and 5, and whether they were maintainable under settled legal principles. The Court found that the issue of maintainability must be decided first by the High Court before proceeding to merits.
legal_provisions_cited: Jharkhand High Court (Public Interest Litigation) Rules, 2010 (Rules 4, 4A, 4B, 5)
Article 191(9) of the Constitution of India
Section 7(A) and 13(I)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
Section 9 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950
final_judgment: The Supreme Court held that the High Court must first decide the preliminary objection regarding the maintainability of the PILs before proceeding to the merits, and accordingly directed the High Court to address the issue of maintainability at the next hearing.
